Glory is an Imperial I-class Star Destroyer and the personal flagship of Grand Admiral Demetrius Zaarin, mastermind of the Empire’s advanced starfighter programs including the TIE Avenger, TIE Defender, and TIE Experimentals. Once a visionary leader within the Imperial Navy, Zaarin betrayed the Empire in a failed attempt to assassinate Emperor Palpatine. Now branded a traitor, he is relentlessly hunted by Darth Vader and Grand Admiral Thrawn.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 35000 (200/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x1 Medium Ion Cannon, x2 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x3 Triple Medium Turbolaser, x6 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 ASF Missile Launcher, x10 Light Ion Cannon, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x28 Dual Turbolaser

Complement: 3 TIE Bizarro Squadron (9)

Predominant is a Imperial-1-class Heavy Star Destroyer and flagship of Grand Admiral Demitrius Zaarin. He is the leader of the TIE Experimental program, and spawns 2 (4) TIE Bizarro squadrons instead of TIE/LN squadrons. Grand Admiral Zaarin is escorted by 2 Captains, each commanding a Vindicator-class frigate equipped with TIE Bizarros.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 35000 (200/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x1 Medium Ion Cannon, x2 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x3 Triple Medium Turbolaser, x6 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x28 Dual Turbolaser

Fleet commander: Admirals are able to increase combat performance of corvettes, frigates, capitals, battlecruisers and dreadnaughts, boosting their shield strength by 10% and movement speed by 20%.

Always stacks with other fleet commander bonuses, but not multiple admirals.

The EF76 Nebulon-B is a light escort frigate mass-produced by Kuat Drive Yards. Originally intended for the Imperial Navy, it instead became a cornerstone of the fledgling Rebel fleet. Armed with medium and heavy laser cannons as well as several turbolasers, the EF76 can assist in fighter screening and provide limited fire support against larger targets.

Protector is a Victory-class Star Destroyer under the command of the trecherous Imperial Admiral Harkov. A proponant of the TIE Avenger Program and a dealer of Imperial arms, Harkov and his personal force of the Nebulon-B Frigates Akaga, Kagi, Siryu, and Horyu join other defectors to dethrown the Emperor and his supporters.

Avenger is one of the first Imperial II-class Star Destroyers to enter service with the Imperial Navy, now under the command of the cunning and traitorous Moff Kalast. Though he poses as a Rebel sympathizer and operates under the alias "Falast" within the Bothan Spynet, Kalast harbors no love for the Rebellion. He sells them just enough information to earn their trust—while manipulating them to serve his own ends. In truth, Kalast has aligned himself with the Imperial Defectors, including fellow traitors like Sait andl Zaarin. Avenger has been reconfigured to deploy a mix of captured Rebel starfighters in place of standard TIEs, transforming it into a versatile and unconventional strike carrier for the growing defector fleet.

Using Bothan tech Avenger's computers can hack enemy ships to disrupt their systems and selling to the Rebel Alliance has granted Kalast access to what are usually Rebel Starfighters

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 45000 (350/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x4 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x8 Octuple Medium Turbolaser, x9 Dual Ion Cannon, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Heavy Laser Cannon, x20 Light Turbolaser, x20 Dual Turbolaser

Complement: 1 X-Wing Squadron (1), 1 A-Wing Squadron (1), 1 Y-Wing Squadron (1), 1 Cutlass Squadron (1)

An up-and-coming Imperial Navy officer from Axxila, Captain Firmus Piett commands a small home fleet and is known for getting results from those under him. A by-the-book officer, Piett is loyal, reliable, and, perhaps to a fault, predictable.

Self-styled Grand Admiral Andal Sait is a traitor to the Empire, having stolen a prototype Vector-class Star Carrier—a heavily modified Star Destroyer designed as a supercarrier for mass starfighter deployment. His flagship, Blackguard, carries thousands of TIE variants, including Defenders, Avengers, TIE/D droid craft, and experimental Bizarros. Sait’s battle doctrine is simple: overwhelm the enemy with an unrelenting swarm of fighters.

Max speed: 3.5; Shield points: 50000 (350/s); Hit points: 70000

SP: 10000 (25/s), HP: 10000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.095 Sensor Range: 3000m, Max Engagement Range: 7000m Active Abilities: Sensor Ping Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x6 Concussion Missile Launcher, x10 Heavy Proton Missile Launcher

Kuat Drive Yards Broadside-class Siege Platform is a specialized mobile launch system equipped with long-range heavy proton missiles capable of bypassing shields and inflicting devastating hull damage on starships and space stations. It also carries standard concussion missiles, providing limited self-defense and general-purpose strike capability.

Despite its heavy armor and formidable payload, the Broadside lacks any form of laser weaponry and relies entirely on escorts for protection. Its concussion missiles, while powerful, are launched in slow volleys and are poorly suited to counter sustained starfighter or bomber attacks. More a strategic asset than a conventional warship, it excels in both offensive ambushes and defensive operations, delivering sustained long-range firepower against advancing enemies.

This starship costs 200 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Special Structures (Empire): E_Shipyard_2

SP: 10000 (100/s), HP: 10000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.2 Sensor Range: 3000m, Max Engagement Range: 3000m Active Abilities: Deploy Master Repair Droids, Deploy Laser Defense Satellite Passive Abilities: Integrated Master Repair Droids, Fleet Logistics Support

Weapons: x2 Dual Turbolaser, x2 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon

Complement: 1 Shuttle Squadron (1), 2 TIE Fighter Squadron (2)

Originally developed by the Republic, the MTC (Modular TaskForce Cruiser) was engineered to provide a broad range of logistical and support capabilities through interchangeable mission modules. These modular systems allow the vessel to be rapidly reconfigured for roles including disaster relief, post-combat search and rescue, repair and salvage operations, planetary suppression and pacification, and deep-space exploration. The MTC is also capable of conducting extensive resource surveys, enabling the evaluation of newly charted systems for colonization and development. In combat, the MTC’s slow speed and poor maneuverability leave it virtually defenseless, restricting its deployment to rear-area support roles under the protection of a larger fleet.

Fleet Logistics and Repair Module: Reduces construction cost and build time by 15% (Corvettes), 10% (Frigates), and 5% (Capital Ships) on the planet this MTC is stationed over. Bonuses do not stack. In combat, Master Repair Droids repair friendly units in an area around the MTC and can be deployed to provide repairs at extended range.

Required Planets (Empire, Warlords): Allanteen, Corellia, Fondor, Kuat, Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana
Special Structures (Empire): E_Shipyard_2
Special Structures (Warlords): Minor_Shipyard_Warlords

SP: 100000 (750/s) HP: 115000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.15, Agility: 0.055 Sensor Range: 4650m, Max Engagement Range: 5250m Active Abilities: Heavy Tractor Beam, Overcharge Weapons (Ion Cannons) Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x2 Proton Torpedo Launcher, x3 Triple Heavy Turbolaser, x6 Triple Heavy Ion Cannon, x8 Dual Ion Cannon, x12 Quad Medium Turbolaser, x24 Light Turbolaser, x42 Dual Turbolaser, x48 Heavy Concussion Missile Launcher

Complement: 3 TIE/D Starfighter Squadron (6)

Designed by Kuat Drive Yards at the request of the Imperial Navy, the Allegiance-class Heavy Star Destroyer was created to counter the rising threat of powerful Mon Calamari cruisers and other heavily armed capital ships. Sacrificing versatility for overwhelming firepower, the Allegiance was purpose-built for direct, sustained fleet engagements. It mounts an array of heavy and medium turbolasers, heavy triple ion cannons, and heavy concussion missile launchers, all protected by thick armor plating and powerful shield generators. The Allegiance excels at anchoring a battle line or spearheading assaults through the enemy center with sheer brute force.

Despite its immense combat power, the Allegiance carries only a small starfighter complement and no dedicated point-defense weaponry. While capable of fending off isolated attacks, it remains vulnerable to concentrated bomber strikes and relies heavily on dedicated escort vessels for protection. Its enormous production cost in both manpower and materials ultimately limited construction to a relatively small number of ships.

The Gladiator-class Strike Carrier is a late Clone Wars–era design from Kuat Drive Yards, developed as a general-purpose carrier and heavy frigate. Equipped with large internal hangars for a substantial starfighter complement, the Gladiator combines fleet support capabilities with respectable frontline firepower. Though not intended for prolonged combat against heavier warships, its versatile arsenal of ion cannons, armor-piercing missiles, and turbolasers allows it to overwhelm corvettes and lighter frigates with ease. Compact, flexible, and heavily armed for its size, the Gladiator remained effective long after the Clone Wars and continued to serve throughout the reign of the Empire.

The "Shield Buster" variant of the Imperator-class Star Destroyer was an experimental design that trades its eight main batteries for a set of devastating long-range broadside octuple heavy ion cannons for dedicated anti-shield firepower. While capable of laying down an immense amount of ion-based firepower on either side of the ship, it is otherwise unremarkable in any other role than that of a support role; it was never intended to be the flagship of a fleet but rather to suppliment and support other warships against heavily shielded opponents. While it excels phenomenally in its intended role, the Shield Buster is considered by many in the Imperial Navy to be a gimmick and was wildly unpopular. Ultimately, few of these specialized warships were built before dissenting voices in the higher echelons of the Navy put an end to its production.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 62250; 2 TIE/D Fighter (4), 1 TIE/D Bomber (2)

The unmistakable symbol of Imperial might and authority, the Imperial I-class Star Destroyer is the backbone of the Imperial Navy and the embodiment of its doctrine of overwhelming force. Evolved from the Clone Wars-era Imperator-class, it features reinforced armor, a more powerful shield generator, and increased firepower. Towering over enemy vessels, it serves as both a warship and a tool of political intimidation.

Its primary batteries, mounted along the flanks, are optimized for broadside engagements due to their lack of superfiring capability. The ship is equipped with numerous laser cannons to defend against starfighters, along with a limited point defense system designed to intercept incoming missiles and torpedoes. The Imperial I remains a powerful frontline warship, capable of anchoring any battle line through sheer presence and sustained firepower.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 35000 (200/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x1 Medium Ion Cannon, x2 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x3 Triple Medium Turbolaser, x6 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x20 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x28 Dual Turbolaser

Complement: 2 TIE/D Starfighter Squadron (4), 1 TIE/D Starbomber Squadron (2)uadron (1)

Building on the foundation of the Imperial I, the Imperial II was designed to for extreme ship-to-ship combat. While retaining the same overall hull design and structural integrity, the ISD-II boasts significantly improved shielding and a more powerful shield generator, greatly enhancing its endurance in prolonged engagements. Its main batteries have been upgraded to octuple turbolaser barbettes mounted to allow superfiring arcs, enabling it to concentrate all of its firepower directly forward—dramatically increasing its offensive output in head-on engagements.

The ISD-II also features a vastly expanded suite of ion weaponry, giving it the ability to quickly overload enemy shields. Its anti-starfighter suite has been overhauled with light turbolasers and heavy laser cannons better suited for engaging corvettes and gunships. To counter bomber strikes, the Imperial II is equipped with a long-range point defense system, offering limited but reliable protection. A focused brawler, the Imperial II excels when leading the charge in heavy fleet battles.

Max speed: 3; Shield points: 45000 (350/s); Hit points: 80000

Weapons: x2 Quad Heavy Ion Cannon, x4 Dual Heavy Ion Cannon, x8 Octuple Medium Turbolaser, x9 Dual Ion Cannon, x10 Ion Cannon, x12 Heavy Laser Cannon, x20 Light Turbolaser, x20 Dual Turbolaser

Special Structures: Minor_Shipyard_Warlords

Fighter 20·Bomber 20·Gunship 10·Transport 10·Corvette 10·Frigate 10·Capital 10·SpaceStructure 10·Super 10

SP: 30000 (200/s) HP: 50000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.12 Sensor Range: 4000m, Max Engagement Range: 4500m Active Abilities: Overcharge Weapons (Heavy Turbolasers), Medium Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x2 Heavy Proton Torpedo Launcher, x2 Quad Medium Ion Cannon, x3 Triple Heavy Turbolaser, x4 Ion Cannon, x8 Quad Turbolaser, x12 Heavy Laser Cannon, x22 Light Turbolaser, x24 Heavy Concussion Missile Launcher

Nicknamed the “pocket destroyer,” the Procursator-class was Kuat Drive Yards’ attempt to distill the raw destructive power of an Imperial Star Destroyer into a smaller, more economical frame. Designed exclusively for ship-to-ship combat, it carries no unnecessary systems or multi-role accommodations—only firepower. Bristling with heavy, standard, and light turbolasers, supported by laser cannons, ion cannons, and batteries of heavy proton torpedoes and concussion missiles, the Procursator can tear apart capital ships with terrifying efficiency. Like its larger counterparts, it boasts thick armor plating, powerful shield generators, and a long-range tractor beam, making it a formidable opponent in direct engagements.

However, its strengths are matched by a critical weakness: the complete absence of a hangar and limited point-defense coverage leave it highly vulnerable to bomber strikes. Imperial doctrine forbade Procursators from operating without a dedicated escort screen of frigates and corvettes—a directive so strict that captains who ignored it sometimes paid with their lives. In the right fleet, the Procursator is a precise, brutal instrument. Alone, it is a hunter that quickly becomes the hunted.

Required Planets (Empire, Rebel, Underworld): Kuat, Fondor
Special Structures (Empire): E_Shipyard_1
Special Structures (Rebel): R_Shipyard_3
Special Structures (Underworld): U_Shipyard_3
Special Structures (Warlords): Minor_Shipyard_Warlords

SP: 30000 (200/s) HP: 50000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.12 Sensor Range: 4000m, Max Engagement Range: 4500m Active Abilities: Overcharge Weapons (Heavy Ion Cannons), Medium Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x2 Heavy Plasma Torpedo Launcher, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x3 Octuple Heavy Ion Cannon, x4 Turbolaser, x8 Quad Turbolaser, x12 Heavy Laser Cannon, x22 Light Turbolaser, x24 Heavy Ion-Pulse Missile Launcher

Nicknamed the “Shieldbreaker,” this dedicated support variant of the Procursator trades its primary armament for three long-range octuple heavy ion cannon turrets, delivering devastating anti-shield firepower and the ability to continuously disable enemy capital ships. Further sacrificing versatility to specialize in this role, heavy Ion-Pulse missiles replace concussion missiles, while heavy plasma torpedoes take the place of proton torpedoes. Exceptionally effective at stripping shields and suppressing enemy systems, the Shieldbreaker is incapable of dealing meaningful hull damage and remains highly vulnerable to bomber attacks.

Required Planets: Kuat, Fondor
Special Structures: Minor_Shipyard_Warlords

Reserve max: 1x TIE_Droid_Squadron, 1x TIE_Droid_Bomber_Squadron

Commissioned by the Republic Navy and built by Kuat Drive Yards, the Victory I-class was developed as a heavy fire-support platform to complement the more versatile Venator. Its heavy turbolaser batteries, paired with armor-piercing missile launchers, gave it a clear advantage in frontline engagements, allowing it to punch through capital ship armor. Its heavy concussion missile system, meanwhile, proved devastating against droid starfighter swarms—threats the Venator struggled to counter effectively. After the rise of the Empire, the Victory I remained in active service, performing exceptionally well against the lightly equipped fleets of the early Rebellion. However, as the conflict escalated and the Rebels deployed more heavily shielded Mon Calamari cruisers and advanced strikecraft, the Victory I became increasingly outmatched and was gradually relegated to secondary theaters of war.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 25000

Weapons: x1 Heavy Ion Cannon, x1 Quad Turbolaser, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x4 Heavy Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x7 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser, Heavy Concussion Missile System (24 missiles)

Complement: 1 TIE/D Starfighter Squadron (1), 1 TIE/D Starbomber Squadron (1)

Developed by Sienar Fleet Systems, the Vindicator-class was designed to fill a role often neglected by the Tarkin Doctrine: a medium-sized, general-purpose heavy frigate. Armed with accurate long-range heavy turbolasers supported by standard and light turbolasers, ion cannons, and heavy laser cannons, the Vindicator can engage and defeat a wide range of targets with ease. Its effectiveness in combat quickly led to widespread production across Imperial shipyards, making it a common sight in major theaters of the Galactic Civil War.

Although heavily armed for its size, the Vindicator's concentrated firepower comes at a cost. Its primary weapons have a relatively slow rate of fire, while its poor shield regeneration leaves lone Vindicators vulnerable during extended firefights. Instead, they perform best when operating in coordinated groups known as “wolf packs,” using accurate long-range firepower to wear down enemy formations before closing to finish the kill.

An unconventional strike group formed from all four prototypes of Admiral Zaarin’s TIE Bizarro program: the TIE Turbo, TIE Stunner, TIE Warhead, and TIE Payload. Each fighter in the squadron serves a specialized role — the Turbo provides long-range firepower with its light turbolaser, the Stunner disables targets with powerful ion blasts, the Warhead saturates the field with concussion rockets, and the Payload unloads devastating proton torpedo salvos. Individually flawed but collectively dangerous, this bizarre mix of experimental starfighters can overwhelm even hardened defenses with sheer firepower and versatility — if they survive long enough to deliver it.

The TIE Payload is the final installment in Admiral Zaarin’s TIE Bizarro program. Featuring a modified TIE Bomber cockpit module, it replaces the standard ordnance pod with two massive pods mounted on either side. Each pod is capable of launching a devastating volley of proton torpedoes, making the TIE Payload a formidable threat to capital ships. However, its sheer size and slow handling make it an easy target for enemy fighters and defenses, limiting its effectiveness in a fast-paced dogfight. While deadly against large ships, the TIE Payload’s vulnerability in close-quarters combat makes it a high-risk, high-reward unit.

The TIE Defender represents the absolute peak of Imperial starfighter development, integrating cutting-edge technology into a single, uncompromising space superiority platform. Armed with multiple laser cannons capable of unleashing a withering barrage, paired with ion cannons, missile launchers, and proton torpedoes, the Defender is lethal against fighters and capital ships alike. Unlike earlier TIE designs, it features heavy armor, powerful shields, a hyperdrive, and exceptional maneuverability driven by its unique triple ion engine configuration. Designed with no regard for cost or ease of production, the TIE Defender is devastatingly effective but prohibitively expensive, ensuring its deployment remained limited despite its overwhelming performance.

The TIE/D Automated Starfighter, commonly known as the TIE Droid, is an advanced Sienar Fleet Systems design that replaces the standard TIE pilot with Cybot Galactica’s Ace-6 droid brain. Reinforced armor, high-efficiency solar arrays, and upgraded ion engines allow the TIE/D to perform extreme maneuvers impossible for organic pilots, granting it exceptional agility and a top speed that surpasses even the TIE Interceptor. Designed to operate in coordinated swarms, the TIE Droid is capable of overwhelming enemy fighters through sheer maneuverability and numbers.

However, despite its mechanical advantages, the Ace-6 droid brain suffers from inconsistent targeting accuracy and poor individual decision-making compared to trained pilots. Combined with its exorbitant production cost, these flaws limited the TIE/D’s adoption within the Galactic Empire. While it saw little official Imperial service, the design found a second life among Imperial Defectors, who leveraged their wealth and lack of manpower to field the TIE Droid as a frontline starfighter in significant numbers.

These improvements grant the craft greater durability and maneuverability than its piloted predecessor. Armed with a heavy laser cannon and ion torpedoes, the TIE/D Starbomber is capable of crippling corvettes and capital ships through coordinated strike attacks.

Despite its enhanced performance, the Ace-6 droid brain lacks the accuracy and adaptability of a trained pilot, and its high cost prevented adoption by the Imperial Navy. Instead, the design saw use among Imperial Defectors, who relied on droid starfighters as frontline strike craft due to manpower shortages or ideological preference.

A relic of strategic compromise, the Ton-Falk-class was designed to supplement Imperial capital ships that embodied the controversial Tarkin Doctrine: prioritizing overwhelming firepower at the expense of starfighter support. With the era of massive fleet carriers like those of the Clone Wars behind them, the Empire turned to the Ton-Falk: essentially a flying hangar bay outfitted to launch and recover hundreds of TIE fighters. Lightly armored, sluggish, and minimally armed with only a handful of medium and heavy laser cannons, plus a rear-mounted concussion missile launcher for defense, the Ton-Falk is ill-suited for direct combat. However, it excels in its intended role: flooding the battlespace with relentless waves of TIEs, providing critical fighter coverage for otherwise vulnerable Imperial warships.

Once a proud vessel of the Imperial Navy, this Venator-class Star Destroyer now serves the enemies of the Empire. Its captain broke his oath and defected, joining the scattered ranks of warlords and traitors opposing Imperial rule. Though aging and stripped of official support, the ship remains operational thanks to hasty retrofits and salvaged parts. Like most defector vessels, it lacks trained crew and instead relies on swarms of TIE Droids to fill its hangars. These autonomous fighters may lack finesse, but they need no pilots, no rest, and no loyalty. This rogue warship now prowls the edges of Imperial space—a dangerous symbol of rebellion flying a different flag.

Designed by Sienar Systems during the final years of the Republic, the Imperial Patrol Vessel-1 (IPV-1) was developed to replace the aging Gozanti-class, whose limited combat capabilities left it vulnerable to droid starfighters and pirate raiders. Featuring improved armor, shields, speed, maneuverability, and firepower, the IPV quickly became the Empire's standard local patrol craft and fleet escort.

Though lacking a hyperdrive and therefore restricted to system defense, the IPV was equipped with a short-range point-defense system capable of intercepting incoming missiles and torpedoes, allowing it to protect both itself and nearby allies. As newer escort ships such as the Tartan Patrol Cruiser and YE-4 Gunship entered service, the IPV was gradually retired, with many finding second lives among pirates, private security firms, and planetary defense forces.

The Acclamator II-class Assault Ship was developed by Rothana Heavy Engineering as a cost-effective modernization of the original Acclamator. Improved armor, stronger shields, and an upgraded weapons suite including quad light turbolasers, quad heavy laser cannons, ion cannons, and advanced proton torpedo launchers greatly enhanced the vessel's combat effectiveness while preserving its role as a heavily armed troop transport. The result was a far more capable frontline heavy frigate without the expense of developing an entirely new class of warship.

SP: 2500 (30/s) HP: 3250, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 4.5, Agility: 0.65 Sensor Range: 1850m, Max Engagement Range: 3000m Active Abilities: Power To Weapons Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x4 ASC Missile Launcher, x4 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x4 Dual Light Turbolaser

Developed by Kuat Drive Yards shortly before the Clone Wars, the Arquitens-class was quickly integrated into the Republic Navy and saw widespread deployment across nearly every major theater. Originally intended for patrol, picket, and escort duties, the Arquitens proved highly adaptable in frontline engagements. Armed with light turbolasers, heavy laser cannons, and anti-strikecraft concussion (ASC) missiles, it is well equipped for both ship-to-ship combat and fighter screening.

What sets it apart from other corvettes of the era is its impressive speed and agility, allowing it to chase down fleeing targets and reposition quickly in battle. With a balanced mix of firepower, mobility, and moderate durability, the Arquitens serves as a flexible all-rounder capable of fulfilling many roles, though exceptional in none.

Required Planets (Rebel, Underworld): Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

The Carrack-class light frigate is a compact, well-armed warship capable of engaging a wide range of targets. Equipped with anti-shield, anti-ship, and anti-starfighter weaponry, it poses a serious threat to corvettes, frigates, and strikecraft alike. However, its relatively weak reactor and shield generator limit its durability in prolonged engagements.

Designed for efficiency and ease of production, the Carrack serves well as an escort vessel and excels when deployed in wolfpack formations, where its versatile loadout and ion weaponry can overwhelm larger targets.

Required Planets: Kuat, Coruscant, Ringo_Vinda, Rendili, Rothana, Allanteen

The Dreadnaught-class, officially designated the Rendili Support Cruiser, is a modern refit of a venerable pre-war Republic cruiser. Armed with a variety of turbolasers, laser cannons, ion cannons, and missiles, the Dreadnaught serves as a well-balanced, general-purpose heavy frigate suited for frontline assaults, fire support, and escort duty. A respectable starfighter garrison and tractor beam projector further enhance its versatility, while thick armor plating allows it to absorb a surprising amount of punishment. Despite these strengths, its weak shield generator, broadside-focused main armament, slow speed, and poor maneuverability leave it at a disadvantage against more modern warships.

Designed and built by Corellian Engineering Corporation prior to the Clone Wars, the Gozanti-class is a rugged and versatile workhorse long used by both the Republic and the Imperial Navy. Primarily an armed transport, the Gozanti can carry starfighters or light vehicles directly into combat using quick-release clamps mounted beneath its hull, allowing it to rapidly deploy and recover assets in contested space.

Armed with forward-firing proton torpedo launchers and twin heavy laser turrets providing near-total coverage, the Gozanti is capable of striking hardened targets or defending itself against enemy bombers. Deployable starfighter repair droids and onboard astromech systems allow it to support nearby fighters while maintaining its own combat readiness. Though slow and cumbersome, with a large and easily targeted profile, the Gozanti remains a valuable fleet support vessel where flexibility and endurance matter more than speed.

Designed and produced by Rendilli StarDrive decades before the Clone Wars, the Neutron Star–class was an early Republic-era frigate intended to serve dual roles as both a warship and a bulk transport. Often referred to simply as a “bulk cruiser,” the class became a common sight along major trade routes and patrol sectors, its silhouette familiar enough to be casually dismissed by smugglers and spacers alike. By the time of the Clone Wars, however, the design was already showing its age, having been eclipsed by newer and more capable Rendilli warships such as the Dreadnaught-class Heavy Cruiser. As a result, the Neutron Star saw only limited frontline service and was largely relegated to secondary duties.

During the Galactic Civil War, the Neutron Star endured as a cheap and readily available alternative to modern capital ships, pressed into service by the Empire and local defense forces for patrol and anti-piracy operations. Armed with several triple turbolasers and numerous heavy laser cannons, it is capable of delivering steady, sustained fire, but its complete lack of ion weaponry or missile launchers leaves it poorly suited to engaging heavily shielded or armored opponents. Mediocre armor protection, merely adequate shields, and a small starfighter complement further underscore its limitations. Long obsolete as a true warship, the Neutron Star nonetheless lives on in widespread use among criminal syndicates and paramilitary forces, valued not for its strength, but for its availability, simplicity, and low cost.

SP: 200000 (1000/s) HP: 450000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.025 Active Abilities: Full Salvo (Turbolasers) Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x3 Dual Medium Laser Cannon, x3 Heavy Proton Torpedo Launcher, x4 Heavy Concussion Missile Launcher, x16 Quad Turbolaser, x38 Heavy Ion Cannon, x42 Heavy Laser Cannon, x66 Dual Turbolaser

Complement: 4 TIE Fighter Squadron (12), 4 TIE Bomber Squadron (12), 4 Tartan Gunship Squadron (6)

Functioning as Admiral Tallon’s command ship, the Battalion is a Praetor-class battlecruiser known for its service against Separatist holdouts. Adar Tallon is a highly successful admiral who began his career in the Republic Navy and fought in the Clone Wars and even helped the Empire hunt down and destroy separatist holdouts but was notably disconcerted by the direction of the New Order and was especially wary of the leadership of Palpatine and Tarkin. Eventually, Admiral Tallon defected, vowing to destroy what he sees as an illegitimate military coup of the Republic that he served...

Initially developed as an upgrade to the Victory I-class, the Victory II ultimately evolved into a distinct platform with a specialized battlefield role. Where the Victory I excels at breaching armor with heavy turbolasers and high-yield warheads, the Victory II is engineered to counter heavily shielded vessels. Its powerful ion cannon arrays can rapidly drain enemy shields, while heavy mag-pulse missile launchers disable critical systems, leaving hostile ships vulnerable to allied attacks. Though it lacks the raw firepower to reliably engage heavily armored capital ships, it remains more than capable of overwhelming enemy frigates and lighter warships. The Victory II also retains its predecessor’s heavy and medium laser cannon batteries, providing a moderate level of anti-starfighter defense against bomber strikes. Quickly becoming a mainstay of the Imperial Navy, the Victory II serves as a valuable force multiplier—working in tandem with its older cousin to counter Rebel threats across the galaxy.

Max speed: 2.75; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 30000

Weapons: x3 Dual Ion Cannon, x4 Heavy Mag-Pulse Missile Launcher, x5 Quad Medium Ion Cannon, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x8 Quad Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser

Complement: 1 TIE/D Starfighter Squadron (1), 1 TIE/D Starbomber Squadron (1)

SP: 8500 (75/s); HP: 12000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.45 Sensor Range: 2650m, Max Engagement Range: 3500m Active Abilities: Redirect Power To Weapons Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

x1 Heavy LRAS Missile Launcher, x3 Medium Turbolaser, x4 High-Velocity Heavy Laser Cannon, x9 Medium Laser Cannon

Before the introduction of the famed Victory-class Star Destroyer, Kuat Drive Yards produced the Victory-II (V-2) “Longbow,” an early pre-war escort and support frigate designed to fill a niche role in the Republic Navy. Armed with three long-range medium turbolaser turrets, the Longbow provided accurate, sustained fire beyond the effective range of most opponents, supporting heavier warships and bomber formations from the rear. Its primary mission, however, was starfighter defense, achieved with several medium laser cannons, four high-velocity heavy laser cannons, and a bow-mounted heavy LRAS (Long-Range Anti-Starfighter) missile launcher that made frontal fighter attacks extremely costly.

Though effective against early CIS droid swarms, the Longbow’s limitations became apparent as more advanced and heavily shielded starfighters entered service. Poor armor protection, weak shielding, and a lack of dedicated ship-to-ship weaponry left the V-2 ill-suited for direct combat, and it was increasingly outclassed in fleet engagements. As naval doctrine evolved, the Longbow was rendered obsolete and gradually phased out in favor of newer, purpose-built anti-starfighter corvettes.

The Corellian Engineering Corporation CR90-class Corvette, often referred to as the blockade runner, is renowned for being among the fastest corvettes ever produced. With its four rapid-fire medium laser cannons and two light turbolaser turrets linked to an advanced fire-control system, the CR90 is an excellent fighter screener and the corvette of choice for Rebel commanders looking to shield their fleets from waves of Imperial TIEs. Although the CR90 is unfit for ship-to-ship combat, it comes equipped with missile-jamming countermeasures and the ability to channel extra reactor power to the engines for a quick escape.

The Defense Penetrator-20 Gunboat, developed by Corellian Engineering Corporation, was designed to supplement the CR90 by taking on a more aggressive combat role. Rather than focusing on fighter screening, the DP-20 emphasizes raw offensive capability with rapid-fire light turbolasers, dual medium laser cannons, and armor-piercing missile launchers. Small, fast, and highly maneuverable, it excels in hit-and-run tactics, darting in to unleash a crippling barrage before retreating beyond enemy firing arcs. However, the DP-20 relies almost entirely on speed for survival, as its armor and shields are extremely weak. When paired with bomber strikes, it becomes a deadly force multiplier capable of tearing holes in enemy capital ships far beyond what its modest size would suggest.

The GR-75 "Gallofree" Medium Transport, named after its manufacturer, Gallofree Yards, Inc., is a rugged, reliable, and above all inexpensive general-purpose utility vessel. Primarily used by the Rebellion, the GR-75 fulfills a wide range of logistical roles, including transport, cargo hauling, refueling, and fleet support. When necessary, it can also serve as a makeshift gunship or fighter screening escort. Outfitted with decent armor but weak shields and underpowered engines, the GR-75 struggles to keep pace with the fleets it supports. Its minimal armament of four dual medium laser cannons is largely forgettable.

This configuration of the GR-75 is dedicated to fleet support, its cargo modules carrying and deploying thousands of repair droids to service nearby friendly vessels.

SP: 36 (3/s), HP: 48 (1/s), Armor: Medium, Max Speed: 3, Agility: 1.725 Active Abilities: Hunt, Lock S-Foils Passive Abilities: Astromech Repair 6 units per squadron.

Weapons: x1 Seeker Torpedo Launcher, x4 Medium Laser Cannon

Medium Laser Cannon: 750 m range, 12 DMG

Seeker Torpedo: 850 m range, tracks target, penetrates shields, damages armor 20 DMG, applies -25% max HP debuff to fighter/bomber/gunship/corvette for 14s

Built by Incom as a true multi-role starfighter, the T-65 X-wing offers a rare balance of durability, firepower, and versatility. Armed with four medium laser cannons and seeker torpedoes, it is capable of engaging enemy fighters, gunships, and even capital ships when required. While its top speed is unremarkable, the X-wing’s S-foils and solid handling allow it to disengage from unfavorable fights when necessary.

Strong shields and an onboard astromech provide the X-wing with excellent staying power in prolonged engagements, allowing it to outlast lighter opponents or wear down enemies suffering from reduced fire rates. However, this resilience comes at the cost of agility. In direct dogfights, the T-65 can be outmaneuvered and overwhelmed by nimble, high-performance interceptors designed specifically for close-range combat. A symbol of the Rebellion across the galaxy, the X-wing remains a dependable workhorse best employed through flexibility, coordination, and smart target selection.
